# coreweave_cks_node_pool (Resource)

Manages a Node Pool in a CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) cluster. The configured provider token must have access to the cluster's Kubernetes API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "coreweave_cks_node_pool" "gpu_workers" {
  cluster_id    = coreweave_cks_cluster.default.id
  name          = "gpu-workers"
  instance_type = "gd-8xh100ib-i128"
  target_nodes  = 2

  compute_class = "default"
  autoscaling   = true
  min_nodes     = 1
  max_nodes     = 4

  labels = {
    workload = "training"
  }

  annotations = {
    "example.com/managed-by" = "terraform"
  }

  taints = [
    {
      key    = "nvidia.com/gpu"
      value  = "true"
      effect = "NoSchedule"
    },
  ]

  update_strategy = "OnSpecUpdate"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the CKS cluster that owns the Node Pool.
- `instance_type` (String) CoreWeave instance type provisioned by the Node Pool.
- `name` (String) Kubernetes name of the Node Pool.
- `target_nodes` (Number) Desired number of Nodes in the Node Pool.

### Optional

- `annotations` (Map of String) Kubernetes annotations applied to every Node in the Node Pool.
- `autoscaling` (Boolean) Whether cluster autoscaling is enabled.
- `compute_class` (String) Immutable compute class for the Node Pool. `spot` Nodes are preemptible.
- `labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes labels applied to every Node in the Node Pool.
- `max_nodes` (Number) Maximum target node count allowed by the autoscaler.
- `min_nodes` (Number) Minimum target node count allowed by the autoscaler.
- `taints` (Attributes Set) Kubernetes taints applied to every Node in the Node Pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--taints))
- `update_strategy` (String) How new Node configurations are staged and rolled out.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier in `<cluster_id>/<name>` form.

### Nested Schema for `taints`

Required:

- `effect` (String)
- `key` (String)

Optional:

- `value` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = coreweave_cks_node_pool.gpu_workers
  id = "{{cluster_id}}/{{name}}"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import coreweave_cks_node_pool.gpu_workers {{cluster_id}}/{{name}}
```
